thread.title: Kano Solar Asset Outperforms 13 Years of DisCo Dividends, MOFI Says
thread.title_full: Kano Solar Asset Outperforms 13 Years of DisCo Dividends, MOFI Says

author: LeadershipNGA
title: Kano Solar Asset Outperforms 13 Years of DisCo Dividends, MOFI Says
text:
MOFI says a small Kano solar asset generated more government revenue in one year than its dividends from Kano DisCo over 13 years, highlighting the commercial potential of renewable energy and the need for professional public asset management.
A small solar power asset in Kano generated more revenue for the Federal Government within 12 months than the dividends it received from its shareholding in Kano Electricity Distribution Company over a period of more than 13 years, according to the Ministry of Finance Incorporated.
The disclosure was made in Abuja during the formal launch of the Renewable Assets Management Company, a new platform intended to manage and commercialise renewable and off-grid electricity infrastructure across Nigeria. The ministry said the striking difference between the two income streams demonstrated the commercial potential of renewable energy and exposed weaknesses in the way public assets and government-linked companies have traditionally been managed. The Kano project was conducted as a pilot in which ownership and operational responsibility were separated.
MOFI retained ownership of the solar asset, while Kano DisCo was responsible for managing its operations. MOFI Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Armstrong Takang said the arrangement produced more revenue in a single year than the government had received in dividends from its investment in the distribution company since the shareholding began. He said the result showed that establishing a professional framework for managing state-owned assets could significantly improve returns and ensure that public resources are used more efficiently.
Takang also questioned the performance of Nigeria's electricity distribution companies. He noted that although an estimated 45,000 megawatts is believed to power economic activity across the country, the DisCos account for only about 6,000 megawatts on the national grid. The gap, he said, indicates that a substantial share of electricity consumption is supplied through off-grid generation.
This situation, combined with persistent challenges in transmission and distribution, is creating space for renewable energy firms and other decentralised power providers to become increasingly important to Nigeria's energy future. He argued that companies such as RAMCO could play a central role in developing and managing the assets needed to expand access beyond the reach of the existing grid.
The new company forms part of MOFI's wider effort to identify government assets, improve the governance of public enterprises and mobilise large-scale private capital for investment. Takang said that when MOFI initially attempted to establish the value of federal government assets, it could verify only about N1.25 trillion. That figure is considerably lower than Nigeria's domestic and foreign debt, which amounts to tens of trillions of naira.
He said the inability to determine what the government owns has made it difficult to optimise those assets, raise financing against them or evaluate whether they are generating appropriate returns. RAMCO is expected to address these issues by combining asset identification, professional management and commercial financing within a single institutional framework.
Takang said the eventual corporatisation of RAMCO and the creation of a stronger balance sheet would help attract institutional investors and other private-sector funding sources instead of relying solely on government allocations. The model is intended to make renewable and off-grid projects more financially sustainable while improving accountability and long-term maintenance.
By separating ownership from management and applying commercial standards, the government hopes to unlock value from existing infrastructure and encourage additional investment in solar power, mini-grids and other clean energy systems. At the launch, Rural Electrification Agency Chairman Ayodele Fayose described RAMCO as a major development for Nigeria's electricity sector. He stressed that building new infrastructure without providing reliable operations and maintenance would undermine the value of public investment.
Fayose called for a stronger sense of ownership among citizens and urged communities to protect electricity facilities so that projects can remain productive for longer periods. His remarks reflected the wider concern that infrastructure sustainability depends not only on construction, but also on effective management, regular maintenance and local support. Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said renewable energy should be regarded as a central part of Nigeria's energy strategy rather than a secondary source of electricity.
The government is targeting 6,500 megawatts of supply by the end of the year and 8,000 megawatts by the end of 2027. It also plans to develop mini-grids in communities affected by transmission shortfalls. RAMCO is expected to support these objectives by improving the reliability, management and commercial viability of renewable assets, while helping to close the gap between electricity access and the financial sustainability required to keep projects operating over the long term
